item.title: hreflang: the right page for each language.
item.description:
Word of the day: hreflang: the right page for each language.
An attribute that tells search engines which language or region each version of a page is for, so a Spanish speaker lands on the Spanish page.
Spot it: Open one translated page and check that it links to every language version, itself included. Google ignores links that are not returned.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=hreflang

item.title: Myth: the padlock means the site is secure.
item.description:
Myth vs fact: Myth: the padlock means the site is secure.
HTTPS encrypts the trip between the browser and the server. It says nothing about the page's scripts, headers and cookies, or about who is behind the site.
Check it: Check what the padlock does not cover: response headers, cookie flags, outdated scripts and a DMARC record.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=myth-https
#WebSecurity #Phishing #CyberSecurity #QA #HTTPS #QAlab

item.title: GOV.CO is empty until JavaScript runs.
item.description:
The portal for more than 78,000 government procedures sends an HTML body with almost no text. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript, so they see a title and little else.
The lesson for every team: Render the main text on the server, or prerender the start page. View source should show what a visitor reads.
One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-2026-10&utm_content=govco

item.title: The BBC decides who may read it.
item.description:

The lesson for every team: Blocking AI training and blocking AI answers are separate choices. Name each crawler in robots.txt on purpose.

item.title: Time your server in one line.
item.description:
30-second trick: Time your server in one line.
curl can report when the first byte of the page arrived. web.dev suggests a Time to First Byte of 0.8 seconds or less for most sites.
Try it now: Run it a few times on your home page and your slowest template. Over 0.8 seconds? Look at the server before the front end.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=evergreen-2026-11&utm_content=ttfb-curl

item.title: Myth: a Lighthouse 100 means accessible.
item.description:
Myth vs fact: Myth: a Lighthouse 100 means accessible.
Lighthouse checks what software can detect, such as names, contrast and ARIA. It cannot tell whether alt text makes sense or whether a screen reader user can finish the task.
Check it: After the score, try one real task with a screen reader: VoiceOver on a Mac, NVDA on Windows.

item.title: We analyzed GOV.UK. It scores 92.
item.description:
Accessibility 100, a strict content security policy, and real visitors see the main content in 0.7 s. The one gap: 19 of the 20 pages analyzed have no canonical link.
The lesson for every team: Give every page a canonical link, even when only one address serves it. One line settles which URL ranks.

item.title: Valle del Cauca locks the pinch-zoom.
item.description:
HSTS runs a full year, framing is limited, and cookies are Secure. But the viewport tag says user-scalable=no, so people who need larger text cannot pinch to zoom on a phone.
The lesson for every team: Drop user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport tag, so people can zoom to at least 200%.
One automated analysis of public pages on 21 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-3-2027-01&utm_content=valle

item.title: Put the mouse away. Can you reach everything?
item.description:
Menus, dialogs, and cookie banners are where keyboard users get stuck. Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, and Escape should be enough.
Try this today: Do your main task on your own site with the keyboard only. Write down every place you got stuck.

item.title: One page, one canonical.
item.description:
When the same content answers at several addresses, ranking signals split between them. Tell search engines which address is the real one.
Try this today: Open your top page with and without a trailing slash and ?utm_ tags. Both should point to one canonical.
How a public-page review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=tips-2026-10&utm_content=canonical

item.title: Scored 31 of 100. The gap: form labels.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But 1987 form controls have no label.
The lesson for every team: Give every input a visible label tied to it with for and id. Screen readers announce it, and the tap target grows.

item.title: indrive.com: 64. The gap: TLS.
item.description:

The lesson for every team: Renew the TLS certificate automatically, and alert well before it expires.

item.title: eep.com.co: 33. The gap: HSTS.
item.description:
12 pages are kept out of search on purpose, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But HSTS is not sent.
The lesson for every team: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a max-age of at least a year, so browsers never try plain http again.
